newsitem.title: USA: GM to increase UAW job security funds - union.
newsitem.headline: GM to increase UAW job security funds - union.

text.p: The United Auto Workers (UAW) union said on Wednesday that General Motors Corp agreed to increase its job security funding by $400 million as part of its new national contract agreement with the union.
The increase will boost an existing $3.35 billion fund, which GM had agreed to carry over from the previous contract. The fund is used to compensate idled workers.

In a document distributed to about 250 UAW leaders gathered here Wednesday, the union disclosed that much of its tentative contract agreement with GM follows the pattern set by Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp.

Although GM's pact calls for the company to maintain hourly employment at 95 percent of current levels, it does allow the company to shift workers between plants in wider geographic areas than under the Ford and Chrysler contracts.
The plant groupings, which will allow GM to replace retiring workers in some plants more slowly than others, are not necessarily as large as the company's Area Hire Groupings.

Area Hire Groupings allow the company to transfer workers within a large area. These areas include, for example, the Flint-Grand Blanc, Mich., area, the Lansing, Mich., area, and the Grand Rapids-Kalamazoo, Mich area.
The document does not identify any parts plants that GM is expected to sell in the near future, nor does it specifically mention the ability of GM to reduce its hourly workforce.
Analysts, however, have said they believe the contract will permit GM to reduce its 215,000-member UAW workforce by as much as 30,000 over the next three years through normal attrition.

The contract also includes new requirements for GM to follow when it wants to shift work to an outside supplier. New rules require GM to notify the union of its parts outsourcing and skilled trade subcontracting plans at an earlier stage to allow the UAW to respond and make an alternative proposal.

The contract calls for workers to receive a $2,000 bonus in the first year, followed by three percent base wage increases in the second and third years. It also increases pension payments for workers under age 62 who retire under the contract by 13 percent to $2,295 a month from $2,030 under the previous contract.
The contract also eliminates a cap on outside earnings for retired workers, which is viewed as an incentive for workers to retire.
